title: Kubernetes workloads
summary: The settings every service on the shared Kubernetes clusters needs so that it cannot harm other services, stays up during maintenance and keeps its secrets safe.
scope: Every deployment, stateful set and job on the shared clusters. Clusters run by a team on its own are out of scope.

resources.title: Helm chart for services
resources.description: Meets every requirement below with safe defaults.

requirements.title: Set resource requests and limits
requirements.statement: Every container sets CPU and memory requests and a memory limit.
requirements.rationale: Without them one busy service takes the capacity of every other service on the same machine.
guidance: Start from the values the platform chart suggests for your kind of service.
Adjust after a week using the dashboard of your namespace.

verification.description: The clusters refuse containers without requests and a memory limit.

lookFor: A container in a manifest with no resources section
A memory request higher than the memory limit

requirements.title: Do not run as root
requirements.statement: Containers run as a non-root user with a read-only root file system and no added Linux capabilities.
requirements.rationale: A break-out from a container running as root gives control of the whole machine.
guidance: Set runAsNonRoot: true and readOnlyRootFilesystem: true.
Write temporary files to an emptyDir volume.

lookFor: runAsUser: 0, privileged: true or allowPrivilegeEscalation: true

requirements.title: Secrets come from Secret Manager
requirements.statement: Workloads get their secrets from Secret Manager through the secrets driver; no Kubernetes Secret with a value is committed to Git.
requirements.rationale: Kubernetes Secrets in Git are only encoded, not encrypted: anyone who can read the repository can read them.
guidance: Mount secrets with a SecretProviderClass that names the Secret Manager secret.
Follow the standard 'Secrets management' for where the secret itself lives.

verification.description: Secret scanner and a policy check on the tenant repositories.

lookFor: kind: Secret with a data or stringData section in a committed manifest

requirements.title: Health checks
requirements.statement: Every long-running container has a readiness and a liveness probe.
requirements.rationale: Without probes, traffic goes to containers that are starting or stuck.
guidance: Use /healthz for liveness and /ready for readiness.

lookFor: A deployment whose containers have no readinessProbe

requirements.title: Survive the loss of one zone
requirements.statement: Critical services run at least three replicas spread over zones, with a disruption budget that keeps two running during maintenance.
requirements.rationale: Cluster upgrades and zone outages would otherwise take the service down.
guidance: Set replicas: 3 and a topology spread constraint on the zone.

verification.description: Weekly report of tier 0 and 1 workloads without a disruption budget.

lookFor: replicas: 1 for a production deployment of a critical service
No PodDisruptionBudget next to a production deployment
